THE LARYNX

- Know the situation of the larynx - Know its cartilaginous parts - Know its ligaments - Know its intrinsic muscles - Know its innervation I-INTRODUCTION: The larynx is an air conduit and the essential organ of phonation. It assumes three functions: - Respiratory, forming part of the respiratory tract. - Swallowing: its closure protects the lower airways. - Organ of sound production: Its phonatory role is very important. It is made up of multiple, mobile cartilaginous parts, between which membranous folds, the vocal cords, are stretched.
A-situation: It is located in the anterior and middle part of the neck, above the trachea, below the hyoid bone and the base of the tongue, behind the thyroid gland.
B-External configuration: In its external form, the larynx is a cartilaginous conduit, easy to identify thanks to the Adam's Apple.
Length: 45mm. Transverse diameter: 45 mm. Sagittal diameter: 40 mm. The dimensions are smaller in women.

C- Constitution: - It is made up of a set of elastic cartilages - Ligaments and joints connecting these cartilages to each other and to neighboring organs. - Muscles - The larynx is covered with a mucous membrane.

1-The cartilaginous skeleton. It includes 3 odd and median cartilages: the thyroid cartilage, the cricoid cartilage, the epiglottic cartilage, 3 even and lateral cartilages: the arytenoid cartilages are the mobile cartilages, the cornicle cartilages and the cuneiform cartilages.

1-1-The thyroid cartilage: The thyroid cartilage is the largest. It is located below the hyoid bone and above the cricoid cartilage. It is formed of 2 symmetrical blades, each in the shape of a quadrilateral, they unite in front, drawing a dihedral angle with posterior sinus, its edge projects forward forming the laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple).
Boudinelabanatlarynx23
The thyroid cartilage has two posterior edges: they extend upwards by the superior horns; and below by the lower horns, the latter articulate with the cricoid cartilage.

1-2-The cricoid cartilage: is located in the lower part of the larynx, above the first tracheal ring. It is shaped like a ring widened towards the rear, made up of a narrow anterior arch and a wider posterior bezel. The latter has a posterior surface where the posterior cricoarytenoid muscle is inserted. A smooth anterior surface. -on each side, on its upper edge, the arytenoid articular surface. - The anterior arch: it presents above its lower edge, the thyroid articular surface.

1-3-The epiglottic cartilage: it constitutes the framework of the epiglottis, it is an approximately vertical strip of elastic cartilage, located above the thyroid cartilage, behind the tongue. It is odd and median in the shape of a racket whose handle is placed in the retracting angle of the thyroid cartilage. Its posterior surface is covered with a mucous membrane which extends over the vocal cords. Its apex is attached to the posterior surface of the thyroid cartilage by the thyroepiglottic ligament. Its base is slightly indented at the top. The epiglottic cartilage acts as a cover for the upper opening of the trachea.

1-4- The arytenoid cartilages: The arytenoids are two small mobile cartilages placed posteriorly, on the lateral parts of the cricoid cartilage, one on the right, one on the left. Shaped like a small triangular pyramid. Each has: - a base, which articulates with the bezel of the cricoid cartilage, - an apex articulates with the corniculate cartilage.
1-5-The corniculate cartilage (Santorini cartilage) It is a small conical cartilage curved inwards. It surmounts each arytenoid cartilage.
1-6-The cuneiform cartilage (Morgagni cartilage) It is a small cartilage located in the ary-epiglottic fold above the corniculate cartilage.
2-1-Cricothyroid joints: They are arthrodia type diarthroses uniting the lower horns of the thyroid cartilage with the thyroid articular surface of the Cricoid cartilage.
2-2-Cricoarytenoid joints: They are Trochoid type diarthroses, the surfaces are convex for the cricoid, concave for the arytenoids.
Boudinelabanatlarynx23

-Cricothyroid ligament: medial it goes from the cricoid cartilage to the thyroid cartilage. -Thyroepiglottic ligament: It runs from the handle of the epiglottic cartilage to the thyroid cartilage. -The fibroelastic membrane: the mucosa is lined by the elastic membrane, which is stretched from the epiglottic cartilage and the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid cartilages. It presents thickenings which are: -The arytenoepiglottic ligament: It goes from the arytenoid cartilage to the epiglottic cartilage. - The superior thyroarytenoid ligament (Ventricular ligament). - The lower thyroarytenoid ligament (Vocal ligament): It is also called the ligament of the vocal cords, forms the framework of the vocal cords and goes from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the vocal processes of the arytenoid.

-The crico-tracheal membrane: Uniting the cricoid cartilage to the first tracheal ring. -The thyrohyoid membrane: It goes from the lower edge of the hyoid bone to the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage, it is reinforced in the middle (median thyrohyoid ligament) and laterally (lateral thyrohyoid ligaments) pierced by the superior laryngeal vasculo-nervous pedicle. -The hyo-epiglottic membrane: It runs from the anterior surface of the epiglottic cartilage to the postero-superior edge of the hyoid bone. 4-the muscles of the larynx:

Intrinsic muscles: all muscles are even except the inter-arytenoid Crico-thyroid, Posterior crico-arytenoid; Lateral cricoarytenoid, the superior thyroarythenoid and the inferior thyroarythenoid (vocal muscle), the arytenoepiglottic The interarythenoid (2 oblique and transverse bundles)

They all insert on the cartilages of the larynx and are all, with the exception of the cricothyroid muscle, located behind the thyroid cartilage. All these muscles modify the lumen of the laryngeal cavity and the vocal cords.
-which close the glottic cleft (constrictors): the lateral cricoarytenoid, the superior thyroarythenoid and the inferior thyroarythenoid, the interarytenoid and the cricothyroid.
Extrinsic muscles: They go from the larynx to neighboring organs, they ensure the elevation of the larynx during swallowing, it is essentially:
- Pharyngeal muscles - the inferior pharyngeal constrictor, the stylopharyngeus and the palatopharyngeus - Neck muscles: the sternothyroid and the sternhyoid.
Boudinelabanatlarynx23

D-Interior configuration. The wall of the larynx is lined with muscle and covered with a thin mucous membrane. Internally, the larynx has three levels that can be identified in relation to the glottis: the cavity where the vocal cords are inserted.
1- The upper, or supraglottic, level is at the height of the epiglottis and its cavity is called the vestibule of the larynx.

2-The middle or ventricular stage is located at the level of the glottis (cavity between the vocal cords). We note on each side on its middle part, two superimposed folds directed from front to back: these are the ventricular bands and the vocal cords. -The ventricular bands: Are formed by the superior thyroarytenoid ligament stretched from the reentrant angle of the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid cartilage. -The vocal cord goes from the same re-entrant angle to the vocal process of the arytenoid cartilage; its thickness contains the inferior thyroarytenoid ligament and the inferior thyroarytenoid muscle. The space between the two vocal cords is the glottic cleft. Between the ventricular bands and the vocal cords a lateral diverticulum is formed: the laryngeal ventricle. 3-The lower level is the subglottic part. This is the end of the tube that leads to the trachea

1-Arterial vascularization: The vascularization of the larynx is provided by three arteries on each side: -the superior laryngeal artery, branch of the superior thyroid artery for the muscles of the larynx and the mucosa of the upper level of the larynx. - the inferior laryngeal artery, branch of the superior thyroid artery, gives branches to the lower level of the larynx. -the posterior laryngeal artery, branch of the inferior thyroid artery, for the mucosa of the posterior surface of the larynx. 2- Venous vascularization: -The superior laryngeal vein and the inferior laryngeal vein go towards the internal jugular vein, via the superior thyroid vein and the thyro-lingofacial trunk. - The posterior laryngeal veins empty into the inferior thyroid vein. 3-The lymphatics of the larynx: The lymphatics of the larynx lead to the jugular lymph nodes

4- Innervation of the larynx: Provided by branches of the vagus nerve - The superior laryngeal nerve: innervates the epiglottis, the mucous membranes of the ventricle and the infra-glottic cavity and the cricothyroid muscle - The recurrent laryngeal nerve innervates all the muscles of the larynx, except the cricothyroid. Unilateral lesion of the recurrent laryngeal nerve causes paralysis of all muscles except the cricothyroid: the voice becomes hoarse.
